When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. (claude.ai sync)","argumentHint":"","aliases":["docs"]},{"name":"anthropic-skills:docx","description":"Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)","argumentHint":"","aliases":["docx"]},{"name":"anthropic-skills:import-memory","description":"Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)","argumentHint":"","aliases":["pdf"]},{"name":"anthropic-skills:pptx","description":"Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. Non-overlapping authorities\n182\t\n183\tThe architecture uses hash-linked bounded authorities instead of one document that duplicates every\n184\tkind of truth:\n185\t\n186\t| Authority                  | Solely owned truth                                                              |\n187\t| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n188\t| Existing Service Catalog   | service identity and runtime/deployment coordinates                             |\n189\t| Data Protection Catalog    | asset scope, owner, RPO/RTO, retention, recovery dependencies, and verifier     |\n190\t| Recovery Cut Manifest      | exact data, release, key, and replica coordinates for one recovery point        |\n191\t| Recovery Operation Journal | typed workflow transitions, fencing generation, and the operation evidence root |\n192\t| Recovery Safety Journal    | post-cut erasure, legal hold, revocation, key, and device-decommission truth    |\n193\t\n194\tEvery authority has a distinct schema and signing policy. References cross authority boundaries by\n195\tstable ID plus content hash; copied fields are rejected by the catalog compiler.\n196\t\n197\t### 2. Data Protection Catalog\n198\t\n199\tAdd one versioned catalog, proposed at\n200\t`infrastructure/data-protection/catalog.yaml`, with a strict JSON Schema and exact-key validation.\n201\tEvery record contains:\n202\t\n203\t- stable `asset_id`, Service Catalog reference, owner, data classification, tenant scope, and\n204\t  legal-hold class;\n205\t- authoritative system and whether the asset is durable or derived;\n206\t- backup mechanism, operational destination, immutable destination, and credential profile;\n207\t- RPO, component RTO, complete-service RTO contribution, retention schedule;\n208\t- encryption algorithm, key authority, key epoch coordinate, escrow authority;\n209\t- recovery dependencies as a directed acyclic graph;\n210\t- cut collector, backup producer, restore handler, reconciliation verifier;\n211\t- source-parity proof and restored-target proof;\n212\t- evidence freshness and drill cadence;\n213\t- destructive-test fixture and cleanup authority;\n214\t- GDPR erase/crypto-shred behavior across retained copies.\n215\t\n216\tEach catalog revision is signed by the retention/compliance owner. Numeric retention, legal-hold,\n217\tand erasure policy are mandatory: there is no default policy. A missing, expired, or unauthorized\n218\tsignature makes readiness `RED`. Discovery performs bidirectional set equality against repository,\n219\tCompose/IaC, live cloud/runtime, and edge-fleet inventories. Unknown assets, duplicated mutation\n220\tauthority, dependency cycles, and durable relationships without a verifier prevent compilation.\n221\t\n222\tThe compiler emits canonical JSON and is byte-idempotent. Two compilations of the same Git SHA and\n223\tinventory snapshot must have identical byte hashes; generated projections cannot contain wall-clock\n224\ttimestamps, filesystem ordering, locale ordering, or provider-list ordering.\n225\t\n226\tGenerated or validated projections include:\n227\t\n228\t- GitHub Environment secret profiles;\n229\t- workflow schedule and concurrency groups;\n230\t- monitoring rules and paging thresholds;\n231\t- runbook asset tables;\n232\t- recovery bundle membership;\n233\t- evidence evaluator requirements;\n234\t- retention/lifecycle configuration;\n235\t- service readiness dependencies.\n236\t\n237\tA CI gate rejects:\n238\t\n239\t- a persistent volume, entity-held object reference, secret epoch, or release artifact with no\n240\t  catalog entry;\n241\t- two mutation authorities for one asset;\n242\t- a durable asset marked as derived without a proven replay source;\n243\t- a recovery dependency cycle;\n244\t- an SLO with no scheduled drill capable of measuring it;\n245\t- a retention class with no legal-hold and erasure behavior;\n246\t- a workflow/runtime path that is not catalog-owned.\n247\t\n248\t### 3. Recovery Control Plane\n249\t\n250\tThe single mutation authority is an offline-capable Rust appliance independent of application\n251\truntimes and the production droplet. Its binary is reproducible; its OCI image is digest-pinned and\n252\tships with SBOM and provenance. A 2-of-3 offline-root-signed TUF bootstrap bundle contains the\n253\tappliance, policy, schemas, trusted clocks/notaries, IaC, and release artifacts needed to start\n254\twithout GitHub, GHCR, or the production droplet. GitHub Actions may request a ceremony but is never\n255\trequired to authorize or execute one.\n256\t\n257\tRequired authority split:\n258\t\n259\t| Identity                      | Allowed                                                   | Forbidden                                                       |\n260\t| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |\n261\t| Production backup writer      | append backup/evidence candidates journal keys; read application plaintext, delete, restore |\n263\t| Evidence notary               | attest object inventory, policy state, and restore result | author host claims, write journal or signed bucket/policy generation | mutate an activated bucket or its policy                        |\n268\t| Organization policy authority | attach a signed SCP digest after offline quorum           | Non-overlapping authorities\n\nThe architecture uses hash-linked bounded authorities instead of one document that duplicates every\nkind of truth:\n\n| Authority                  | Solely owned truth                                                              |\n| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Existing Service Catalog   | service identity and runtime/deployment coordinates                             |\n| Data Protection Catalog    | asset scope, owner, RPO/RTO, retention, recovery dependencies, and verifier     |\n| Recovery Cut Manifest      | exact data, release, key, and replica coordinates for one recovery point        |\n| Recovery Operation Journal | typed workflow transitions, fencing generation, and the operation evidence root |\n| Recovery Safety Journal    | post-cut erasure, legal hold, revocation, key, and device-decommission truth    |\n\nEvery authority has a distinct schema and signing policy. References cross authority boundaries by\nstable ID plus content hash; copied fields are rejected by the catalog compiler.\n\n### 2. Data Protection Catalog\n\nAdd one versioned catalog, proposed at\n`infrastructure/data-protection/catalog.yaml`, with a strict JSON Schema and exact-key validation.\nEvery record contains:\n\n- stable `asset_id`, Service Catalog reference, owner, data classification, tenant scope, and\n  legal-hold class;\n- authoritative system and whether the asset is durable or derived;\n- backup mechanism, operational destination, immutable destination, and credential profile;\n- RPO, component RTO, complete-service RTO contribution, retention schedule;\n- encryption algorithm, key authority, key epoch coordinate, escrow authority;\n- recovery dependencies as a directed acyclic graph;\n- cut collector, backup producer, restore handler, reconciliation verifier;\n- source-parity proof and restored-target proof;\n- evidence freshness and drill cadence;\n- destructive-test fixture and cleanup authority;\n- GDPR erase/crypto-shred behavior across retained copies.\n\nEach catalog revision is signed by the retention/compliance owner. Numeric retention, legal-hold,\nand erasure policy are mandatory: there is no default policy. A missing, expired, or unauthorized\nsignature makes readiness `RED`. Discovery performs bidirectional set equality against repository,\nCompose/IaC, live cloud/runtime, and edge-fleet inventories. Unknown assets, duplicated mutation\nauthority, dependency cycles, and durable relationships without a verifier prevent compilation.\n\nThe compiler emits canonical JSON and is byte-idempotent. Two compilations of the same Git SHA and\ninventory snapshot must have identical byte hashes; generated projections cannot contain wall-clock\ntimestamps, filesystem ordering, locale ordering, or provider-list ordering.\n\nGenerated or validated projections include:\n\n- GitHub Environment secret profiles;\n- workflow schedule and concurrency groups;\n- monitoring rules and paging thresholds;\n- runbook asset tables;\n- recovery bundle membership;\n- evidence evaluator requirements;\n- retention/lifecycle configuration;\n- service readiness dependencies.\n\nA CI gate rejects:\n\n- a persistent volume, entity-held object reference, secret epoch, or release artifact with no\n  catalog entry;\n- two mutation authorities for one asset;\n- a durable asset marked as derived without a proven replay source;\n- a recovery dependency cycle;\n- an SLO with no scheduled drill capable of measuring it;\n- a retention class with no legal-hold and erasure behavior;\n- a workflow/runtime path that is not catalog-owned.\n\n### 3. Recovery Control Plane\n\nThe single mutation authority is an offline-capable Rust appliance independent of application\nruntimes and the production droplet. Its binary is reproducible; its OCI image is digest-pinned and\nships with SBOM and provenance. GitHub Actions may request a ceremony but is never\nrequired to authorize or execute one.\n\nRequired authority split:\n\n| Identity                      | Allowed                                                   | Forbidden                                                       |\n| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Production backup writer      | append backup/evidence candidates to non-journal prefixes | write journal keys; read/delete/restore/administer WORM         |\n| Immutable-vault replicator    | one-way append into named data prefixes                   | write journal keys; read application plaintext, delete, restore |\n| Evidence notary               | attest object inventory, policy state, and restore result | author host claims, write journal or backup objects             |\n| Restore reader                | read an exact approved recovery cut                       | write backup stores or journal; read unrelated epochs           |\n| Recovery controller           | claim journal keys and advance the typed state machine    | write backup data; access user APIs; bypass verifier failures   |\n| Retention administrator       | sign future catalog retention policy under dual control   | possess data credentials; mutate an activated vault generation  |\n| Vault bootstrap quorum        | create and activate a new signed bucket/policy generation | mutate an activated bucket or its policy                        |\n| Organization policy authority | attach a signed SCP digest after offline quorum           | hold member-account data credentials or write journal/data      |\n| Break-glass operators         | authorize a signed recovery request with quorum           | directly run database/object/policy mutation commands           |","numLines":120,"startLine":150,"totalLines":1149}}}

references `infrastructure/data-protection/catalog.yaml` as a surface that 'no longer exists' and that the doc 'answers confidently about a surface that is gone'. The cited line does not do that. PLAN.md:199-200 reads 'Add one versioned catalog, proposed at `infrastructure/data-protection/catalog.yaml`, with a strict JSON Schema and exact-key validation' — the verb is 'Add' and the qualifier is 'proposed at', so the sentence names where a future artifact should live. The document's header at PLAN.md:9 fixes its status as 'Architecture plan; no runtime, deployment, App, secret, or evidence-journal mutation', PLAN.md:10 marks the production claim 'Not ready', PLAN.md:31 states 'This document introduces no runtime behavior', and the Definition of done at PLAN.md:1119-1123 makes 'the Data Protection Catalog covers every persistent or rebuild-critical asset' a completion condition, closed by PLAN.md:1148 'Anything less remains not ready'. Search record at ba4366830605ab4584de58169090cb6b8fde9027: glob `infrastructure/data-protection/**` returned no files, while `infrastructure/**` holds the nats, helm, kubernetes, monitoring, deploy, docker and simulators trees, so the parent directory exists and only the proposed subtree is absent; a repository-wide grep for the exact string `infrastructure/data-protection/catalog.yaml` matches only PLAN.md:200, so no workflow, schema, or consumer in the tree points at the path. A `doc_references_missing_path` true positive requires a document that presents the path as current; this document presents it as a proposal, so the staleness premise fails on the doc's own text.
